newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania "royalty" wedding draws business barons.
newsitem.headline: Romania "royalty" wedding draws business barons.

text.p: Romania got a rare celebrity wedding on Sunday when the self-styled "Prince Paul of Romania" wed commoner Lia Triff in a show attended by some powerful post-communist business barons.
Paul, who claims descent from Romania's King Carol II, is ignored by exiled ex-King Michael but he has won acceptance from authorities reluctant to let the exiled king return.

Lesser-known European aristocracy and local business magnates attended the wedding in a Bucharest church, where star gymnast Nadia Comaneci wed American gymnast Bart Conner in a glittering show staged by the post-communist elite in April.
But political leaders, busy campaigning for the November 3 parliamentary and presidential polls, did not show up on Sunday.

Local tycoon George Paunescu, whose family holdings include hotels, media interests and an airline, was one of two best men and German aristocrat Prince Georg Victor of Bentheim and Steinfurt was the other.
Paunescu and his brother Valentin acted as "godfathers" for the couple, a role traditional in Romanian Orthodox weddings that usually involves support and protection for the couple.
The groom's father, Mircea Carol, who lives in London, was absent.
Last year Paul won a local court battle to have his father recognised as the legitimate first son and heir of Carol. An appeal lodged by ex-king Michael's lawyers is scheduled for next month.

Carol eloped with socialite "Zizi" Lambrino in 1918 and produced a son, Mircea Carol, but the marriage was annulled. He abdicated in 1940, leaving the throne to Michael, born from his marriage to Princess Elena of Greece.

On Sunday, Paul, 48, top hat in hand, wed his 47-year-old American bride in traditional Orthodox style. He said his father would return from self-imposed exile only when "his status is duly recognised".
A prelate translated the religious service into English as an Orthodox priest put two traditional "crowns" on the couple's heads, according to Romanian tradition.
Triff, in a tight satin-and-lace wedding gown, with sapphire earrings to match her deep green eyes, said hers was the "first royalty wedding in Eastern Europe in over 50 years".
The couple call themselves "the Romanian branch of the royal family", irking the exiled royals.
Michael, 74, who lives in Switzerland, was sent into exile by communists who took power in Romania after World War Two.
Post-communist authorities have not allowed him to return since 1992, when he was feted by hundreds of thousands of well-wishers on an emotional Easter homecoming.
Romanian monarchists accuse those associated with the leftist regime of President Ion Iliescu of using Paul as a thorn in Michael's side to deflate his enormous popularity.
"Paul Lambrino never won the right to be part of the royal family," said Simina Mezincescu, a leading royalist.
Michael's eldest daughter, Princess Margareta, is due to wed a commoner, Romanian actor Radu Duda, in a private ceremony in Switzerland next week.
